test:postgres-real.note: Green end to end for the first time. This gate had never completed: it ran tests/omnia-v9-external-effect-state-machine, stopped inside it and waited, so roughly 180 real-database tests scheduled behind that file had never executed and no run ever said so. Three separate causes, each found by removing the one in front of it. (1) The exhaustive transition check made ~600 client round trips; somewhere around the 122nd the connection stopped responding, with the backend `active`, waiting on nothing, holding no lock and ignoring statement_timeout. A pool, then one client, then a connection per pair all stopped in the same place, which is what identified the round trips themselves as the cost. The loop now runs in PL/pgSQL: four statements instead of six hundred, and the client no longer takes any part in deciding what the database accepted. (2) The Gmail concurrency test asserted that exactly one of two workers claimed a row, which was only ever true when the two transactions happened to overlap. On a fast database they stopped overlapping and both claims were legitimate -- RESULT_UNCERTAIN is itself unresolved, so a committed row is a valid candidate again. The overlap is now made real by holding the first worker's transaction open, which tests FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED rather than assuming it. (3) The payment replay test drove a hundred replays from the client; inside node:test, after about a hundred rejected pg queries the next one never returns. Measured four ways before concluding: no conflicts, 200 queries in 61ms; conflicts through a pool, stops at ~55 iterations with no backends left on the server; conflicts on one dedicated client, same ~100; the identical loop outside node:test, 300 conflicts in 90ms. It is the runner, not the driver and not production -- nothing in src/ changed for it. Postgres now runs its own hundred and reports what the index refused. Each suite also gets a private disposable server rather than a database on a shared one, the same isolation the mutation war needed.

test:mutation-war.note: Fully green for the first time, with nothing skipped. Getting there took four defects out of the gate itself, every one of which had been reporting a guard as untested while printing a clean summary line. (1) It read CHROMIUM_PATH and nothing sets it, so a browser guard was skipped on a machine with Chromium installed. (2) SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES meant "nobody handed this run a database", leaving nine guards unexercised wherever a variable was unset; the war provisions its own now, and the skip survives only for a server that will not start. (3) Suites ran with no deadline, so one hang stopped the whole run in ep_poll with no verdict and nothing to say which mutation it was on. (4) All 160 mutations shared one database and then one server, so a suite that left state behind broke every database-backed suite after it -- the gate was measuring the order it visited them in. Each database-backed mutation now gets a private disposable server. The run is also resumable: MUTATION_WAR_JOURNAL records each verdict as it is decided, bound to a hash of the file, anchor, replacement and killing suites so a guard that moved runs again rather than inheriting an answer. Four consecutive runs had been lost to container restarts before that existed. POSTAL-QUARANTINE remains worth recording: anchored on the ledger wrapper's quarantine filter it SURVIVED, because deriveCurrentPostalState filters the same three fields immediately afterwards, so removing the wrapper's copy changes no output for any input. A redundant guard is unfalsifiable. Re-anchored on the filter that decides, it kills.

test:browser.note: This gate caught a P0 this shift: the browser runtime pool integration moved the crawl result variables inside a try block while the return stayed outside it, so every crawl threw ReferenceError. check:syntax parsed it, the deterministic suite does not cover it, and the pool unit tests mock the browser. Only this gate saw it.
